stories.title: How Afghan Women Are Rebuilding Reproductive Health Care
stories.label: health
stories.summary: In parts of Afghanistan where health care has been hard to come by, local women are stepping in to fill the gap. Midwives are running small family health houses in villages, giving pregnant women regular checkups, screening for anemia, and helping them through safe deliveries. One mother, now pregnant with her sixth child, says she finally feels like one of the lucky ones because of the care she's getting close to home. It's a quiet but real example of communities finding ways to protect mothers and babies even in tough circumstances.
stories.why_good: It's a real, ongoing program that is measurably improving maternal health care for women in Afghanistan, not a plan or a study.

stories.title: Wind Turbines Provide Half of Rancher's Income Since He Decided to Invite Them on His Land
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: Back in 2006, a Kansas rancher named Peter Ferrell agreed to let wind turbines go up on his land, and it turned out to be one of the best decisions of his life. Fifty turbines now stand among his Flint Hills pastures, quietly spinning away while his cattle graze right alongside them. The royalties they generate have grown to cover half of his income, money that's helping him pass the family ranch down to his kids. It's a simple story of clean energy and traditional farming working side by side, with everybody benefiting.
stories.why_good: A real, years-long example of renewable energy directly improving a family's livelihood while coexisting with traditional agriculture.
